result.title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
result.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 AI Measurement Science Workshop
result.summary: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting posterior gives exact uncertainty about the modelled success rate without numerical integration or neural inference. A public evaluation covers 79 system-benchmark pairs and eight seeds, reaching Brier ALC 0.200250 for the submitted method. Accompanying code and sufficient statistics reconstruct the fitted prior byte for byte and replay all 632 evaluation trajectories. The result demonstrates how much predictive value a compact Bayesian model can extract from sparse target feedback at very low online cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用公开评测计数构造弱 Beta 先验，再从至多 31 个揭晓结果做精确后验更新，用极小的无神经组件模型预测系统在新基准上的表现，报告 Brier ALC 0.188 与微秒级在线成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏反馈下的精确后验不确定性」可能为 LVR 的停止决策或小样本评测可信度刻画提供形式化借鉴，但该文面向基准分数预测而非推理期状态，迁移可行性需核查。
